attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family with the per-TU flags in configure.py; applies to a run of 2+ adjacent, data-independent statements (no shared variables, no control dependency) where target's disassembly shows one statement's load/compute instructions physically interleaved among the instructions of its neighbor rather than emitted as a separate contiguous block.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC's list scheduler interleaves independent statements' instructions for latency hiding, but which statement's instructions appear FIRST in the interleaved sequence is influenced by the statements' relative order in the SOURCE (AST/IR node order), not purely by data dependency (which permits either order). When target's disassembly shows an independent computation's load+op instructions threaded between an adjacent unrelated statement's own load/op/store instructions, and the current source has that computation positioned textually AFTER its neighbor instead of interleaved-as-if-first, physically moving the whole statement to before its neighbor (still same control-flow position, same block) can reproduce target's interleave exactly. Diagnostic: for a run of independent statements identified via an fndiff --ops cluster showing an opcode-multiset mismatch localized to that run (not a pure register-rename), check the FIRST instruction touching each source variable in target's disassembly against the SAME check in ours; a statement whose first-touch instruction appears earlier in target than in ours (relative to its neighbors) is a reorder-forward candidate. This is a plain statement-order change, distinct from claim.law.declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule (which is about a declaration's initializer vs. an EARLIER store) and claim.law.chained-init-constant-share (which is about merging two initializers of the SAME constant into one chained assignment) - no declaration or initializer is involved here, only the order of two already-declared statements within one block. Gate every reorder individually with fndiff --count (insn-count parity, real-line delta) before accepting, per claim.law.large-fn-batch-fuzzy-can-mask-subfield-regression - a reorder that looks locally plausible from the disassembly alone is not guaranteed neutral elsewhere in a >4000-insn function.
